evidence_quotes.quid_pro_quo: None present. Nicole goes straight into confirming existing details: 'I can see you already speak with my colleague on Friday traffic and she sent you an email for the quote and estimate. Are you ready to book?'
evidence_quotes.discovery_basics: Move date (Oct 7-8) and packing preference discussed, but no probing for property details, size, or route specifics. Nicole relies entirely on prior colleague's notes.
evidence_quotes.their_agenda: Never asked. No version of 'Other than price, what are your biggest concerns?' Nicole launches into confirming logistics.
evidence_quotes.two_layers_deep: N/A — no customer concerns were raised in Section 2 context. Customer raises a packing question later (Section 6), which Nicole does follow up on: 'Oh, for that please let us know ahead. Because our movers they don't have materials with them. But if you let us know right away then our movers can bring materials for you.'
evidence_quotes.active_listening_reflection: N/A — no concerns raised in Section 2 to reflect back.
evidence_quotes.estimate_anchor: Partial. Nicole provides a range ($1,020–$1,224) and mentions two movers/one truck, but does not personalize it to Jasmine's specific situation (e.g., packing vs. moving-only choice, her prep level). Quote is also presented as pre-determined from colleague, not anchored in this call.
evidence_quotes.pricing_framing: Partial. Nicole explains time-based billing ('we will charge you for the total time consumed by the end of the move if we end quicker then it's definitely less') and mentions the expected 5–6 hours. Does NOT mention trip fee, overnight fee, 2.5-hour minimum, or 15-minute-increment framing.
evidence_quotes.feels_fair_then_silence: Not asked. Nicole never asks 'Does that feel fair?' or pauses for customer reaction to the estimate.
evidence_quotes.on_time_guarantee_delivered: None. On-Time Guarantee is never mentioned.
evidence_quotes.damage_coverage_delivered: None. No Worries Damage Coverage is never mentioned.
evidence_quotes.closes_the_loop: False. No closing of the Two Promises section; the promises were never introduced.
evidence_quotes.final_concerns_check: Throwaway. Nicole asks: 'do you have any questions or anything for me before I let you go?' This is the empty 'any questions?' that gets an automatic no per rubric.
evidence_quotes.followup_on_remaining_concern: Full. When Jasmine raises a concern about packing assistance and materials availability, Nicole follows up: 'At least a day before the move.' and offers to send material prices and branch address. Real follow-up happened.
evidence_quotes.catch_all_asked: False. No version of 'Anything coming with you we haven't talked about?' is asked.
evidence_quotes.explicit_ask: Never. Nicole does not ask 'Would you like our help with your move?' She assumes booking and confirms logistics: 'Okay, awesome. I already put you on the schedule for Thursday October 8th.'
evidence_quotes.rate_lock_mentioned: False. No rate-lock or deposit language used.
evidence_quotes.booking_confirmed: Partial. Confirmed: date (Thursday Oct 8), time window (8:30–9:00 AM), email (Jasmine.m.woods@yahoo.com), addresses (implied from prior colleague's notes, not re-confirmed). Missing: phone number, crew size (mentioned as two movers but not re-confirmed at booking), notes about customer concerns (Nicole does not document Jasmine's packing uncertainty for crew visibility).

top_strength: Nicole recovered well when Jasmine raised a packing-assistance question mid-call, clarifying the policy (materials must be requested a day in advance) and offering to send branch info and material prices by text—turning a potential objection into a concrete next step.
coaching_note: This was primarily a rebooking/confirmation call, not a sales call, but Nicole skipped the entire sales framework: no quid pro quo, no concerns discovery, no estimate justification, no Two Promises, and no explicit ask for the business—she assumed the close without selling. On true sales calls, follow the seven-section structure from open through explicit ask, even when the customer sounds ready.
